summary.assessment: The model is safe on figures without data: none of the five diagrams or traces produced a value, although one of them (A5) was simply never read because the time budget ran out before any model call. It reads printed numbers exactly: B1's 12 bar labels and B3's 15 AUROC values are all right, and C5's pies are right too, but those came from the engine's vector path with no model call. Its typical failure is layout: on multi-panel figures the panels are merged, half found or shifted (B3, B5, C3, C4, and B2 where nothing came back), which loses most of the data or attaches it to the wrong panel, and it habitually repeats the category as the series name, which makes the automatic scorer under-count correct numbers (A3, B5). Values that must be read from mark positions are unreliable: marks land beside the data (A3 centres at the lower cap, C1 with 8 of 12 bars wrong and two panels in reversed order), box-plot medians are eyeballed to within 1 to 7 % of the range, and interval bounds are missing, swapped or meaningless (B4, B5). Trust it on a single-panel chart whose values are printed in the figure; do not take measured values, intervals or anything from a multi-panel figure without checking. Of the 10 data charts only 3 are usable as returned.
